To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Arg206 of SNAP- 25 is essential for the fusion of synaptic vescicles with the presnaptic plasma membrane.
Arg206 of Drosophla melanogaster SNAP-25 is an essential component of the neuroexcytotic machinery at the larval neuromuscular synapse.
the highly conserved arginin residue (Arg198) within the C-terminus of SNAP-25 plays an important role in neuroexocyosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the functional role of a conserved residue in the C-terminal region of the SNARE protein SNAP-25, which is essential for the function of the machinery that mediates neuroexocytotic fusion at the neuromuscular synapse.
the molecular mechanisms of neuroexocytic transmission and the identification of the functional domains of proteins that are involved in this process.

the role of a highly conserved residue within the SNAP-25 protein, which is cleavage site for botulinum neurototoxin A and is essential for neurotransmitter release at the Drosophilaneuromuscular junction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arg206 in SNAP-25 is a crucial residue in the fusion of synaptic membranes.
the Arg206Ala substitution of SNAP-25 results in an impaired ability of the protein to assemble into a SNARE complex and that this in turn leads to a defective exocytotic process.
Arg206 of SNAP-24/25 is essential for the function of the SNARE proteins in neuroexocytic fusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P1′ of SNAP-25, which is cleavable by botulinum toxin A, is essential for the function of the SNARE machinery.

the P1′ residue of the SNAP-25 cleavage site by botulinum A neurotoxin is essential for the fusion of synaptic membranes in vivo, and that the P1 and P1′ residues of the SNAP-2 cleavage sites by botulinum B neurotoxin are essential for the fusion and/or priming of synaptic vesicles.
the P1′ residue of the botulinuminotoxin A cleavage motif in SNAP-25 is an essential element of the neuroexocyotosis machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the C-terminal region of the SNAP-25 isoforms is essential for the function of this protein in the assembly of a rosette structure, which is required for the fusion of synaptic and presynaptic membranes during neuroexocytotic release.
the C-terminal region of SNAP-25 plays an essential role during exocytosis at Drosophila neuromuscular synapses.
Arg206 is a critical component of the machinery that regulates the fusion of synaptic-vesicle contents into the presynaptic membrane.
